habitat: Common in the Karoo and very common on the highveld, in parks and gardens. Males display with drooping wings and the tail splayed and dragging on the ground.
summary: A common endemic resident. Much duller than Olive Thrush. It is dark grey-brown, with only the underbelly orange. Throat spotting is absent or vestigial, the vent is greyish and occasionally white, and the bill and legs are orange-yellow. The eye-ring is orange, not brown. Newman does not describe the voice. No Kemp estimate is stored.

similar.note: Olive Thrush is more orange below, with a speckled throat, a dark wedge on the culmen, a brown eye-ring and a white vent.

head.pattern: Throat spotting absent or vestigial. Dark grey-brown.

underparts.pattern: Drab grey-brown, with only the underbelly orange. The vent is greyish, occasionally white.

viewNotes.note: Dark grey-brown, with an orange underbelly and an orange-yellow bill.
Little or no throat spotting. The eye-ring is orange.
Drooping wings and a splayed tail dragged on the ground.
Only the underbelly is orange. The vent is greyish or occasionally white.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The grade A call is from Klerksdorp. The filename also names a sparrow, so another bird may be present. The filename is XC503252-2 Karoo Thrush and sparrow.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common endemic resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Grey-brown and orange-yellow are not stored as single colours. The voice is not described. The grade A call is from North West and its filename names a sparrow. No Kruger photograph was found. No Kemp estimate is stored.
